- White King on f3 (just moved there)
- White Queen on d3
- Black Knight on c2 (actively placed)

The critical insight: **Ne3+** is a royal fork! The knight gives check to the king on f3 while simultaneously attacking the queen on d3. 

After Ne3+, White's king must move (any square: Kg3, Kf2, Ke2, Ke4, Kg4), and Black simply plays Nxd3, winning the queen for just a knight—a decisive material advantage.

**Coaching note:**
Look for knight moves that attack the enemy king. When a knight gives check while also attacking another piece (especially the queen), you've found a royal fork—one of the most powerful tactical patterns. Always scan for checks first; they often hide the best move.
